en.title: How Firm a Foundation
en.author: "K" in Rippon's Selection
stanzas:
How [G]firm a foun[C]dation, ye [G]saints of the [D]Lord,
Is [G]laid for your [C]faith in His [D]excellent [G]word!
What [G]more can He [C]say than to [G]you He hath [D]said—
To [G]you who for [C]refuge to [D]Jesus have [G]fled?

“Fear not, I am with thee, oh, be not dismayed,
For I am thy God, and will still give thee aid;
I'll strengthen thee, help thee, and cause thee to stand,
Upheld by My gracious, omnipotent hand.

“When through the deep waters I call thee to go,
The rivers of sorrow shall not overflow;
For I will be with thee thy trouble to bless,
And sanctify to thee thy deepest distress.

“When through fiery trials thy pathway shall lie,
My grace, all-sufficient, shall be thy supply;
The flame shall not harm thee; I only design
Thy dross to consume and thy gold to refine.

“The soul that on Jesus doth lean for repose,
I will not, I will not, desert to his foes;
That soul, though all hell should endeavor to shake,
I'll never, no never, no never forsake.”

notes: The five commonly-printed stanzas; Timeless Truths and hymnary's representative text carry the same five (Rippon's 1787 original signed "K" — attributed to Robert Keen(e) or George Keith per hymnary — had seven; "E'en down to old age" and one other are rarely printed and not in either consulted source). One variant to know about: stanza 5 line 1 reads "doth lean" in Timeless Truths but "hath leaned" in hymnary's representative text — the consulted source's reading is kept. The opening quotation marks on stanzas 2-5 with the single closing mark at the hymn's end are the source's punctuation (continuing speech), kept as printed. Tune FOUNDATION (American melody, pub. 1832), 11.11.11.11 as hymnary lists it; Timeless Truths also offers ADESTE FIDELES as an alternate — FOUNDATION is shipped. Key: the hymnal key is A-flat (Timeless Truths score); G and A are each one semitone away and FORMAT's preference order picks G. Chords: a standard simplified guitar chart for this pentatonic shape-note tune (I-IV-I-V phrases, lines 1/3 half-cadencing, lines 2/4 resolving); published harmonizations vary more than for most hymns in this set.
